evidenceLayout: evidenceRoot is tmp/plv. This run uses the per-session, per-plan subdirectory tmp/plv/s209/<planId>/ (a retry uses tmp/plv/s209/<planId>/attempt-<n>/). It holds each plan's full command logs; each log ends with an exit=<status> line; each plan's Progress Log records every command, exit status and log path. tmp/ is gitignored. Logs from session 205 under tmp/plv/PLV-*/ are not evidence for this run. A missing or truncated log is not a pass.

executionModel.commitOwner: The orchestrator commits the accepted design and these plans before fanout, and commits the implementation after review. Each commit uses the AGENTS.md numbered 1-6 section message with no Co-Authored-By or tool attribution. Workers never commit, stash, checkout, reset, branch, push or merge.
executionModel.retryPolicy: The waves are serial, so no concurrent plan shares the tree. If cargo reports a lock, wait about 60 s and retry, up to 10 times, then record a blocker and stop.
executionModel.editProtocol: Before each edit, re-read the file and record its sha256 and an intent snapshot. If the file drifted because of a change you did not make, re-read it, re-apply only your own change and record the drift. After editing, record the post-edit sha256. Never edit outside writePaths.
executionModel.serialReconciliation: Each shared path has exactly one owner. PLV-30 alone touches template.rs, build_helpers.rs, voice.rs and voice/lifetime.rs. PLV-31 alone touches templates.vact, the editor template lists, golden_digests.txt (the 24 Plaits graph lines only), the 14 mem_total test files and src/types/tests/inst/templates.rs. PLV-40 alone touches the manifest label, the inventory, the notices, the Plaits plans, the handoff, the README and the design status. Formatting is rustfmt on each plan's own files only. A failing full nextest run is rerun with --no-fail-fast before any repair. Any repair outside a plan's writePaths is recorded as a blocker and applied serially by the orchestrator review step, with file, cause, fix and pre/post sha256.

designDecisionsAndRationale: D-209-1: the seed ordinal is the position in topo_order of the gate-elided graph. Gates are removed and their out-edges redirected to the subject; sources feeding only gate ports >= 1 are removed; the port-0 subject is kept. This is exact for the edit rule and the identity for gate-free graphs.
D-209-2: the gate state stays in the fixed mem region; mem_total +32 per wired template; the pinned tests are updated with the reason.
D-209-3: serial plans with single ownership.
D-209-5: lpg-mode defaults to off, an exact pass-through with the implicit fade kept.
D-209-6: the upstream trigger delay is an effective 4 blocks (1 ms); Vactr has none, so onset timing does not move.
intentionalTradeoffs: lpg-mode defaults to off, so every existing template keeps its render digest; the gated sound is opt-in (D-209-5).
Every wired template gains 2 * GATE_STATE_FLOATS (32) mem floats, even in off mode, in exchange for a fixed, allocation-free gate layout (D-209-2).
The 24 Plaits graph digest lines change because of the new gate nodes, while every render line stays byte-identical; the graph change is justified by the design's gate-elided seed-order section.
Vactr applies no 1 ms trigger delay, so onset timing does not move (D-209-6).
One extra bounded topo_order pass per Template::build computes the seed ordinals; topo_order itself is not changed.
Serial single-owner plans (PLV-30 -> PLV-31 -> PLV-40) instead of parallel fanout, to avoid the unowned-file breakage of session 205 (D-209-3).
supportedEdgeCases: Graphs with no vactrol-gate: the seed ordinal equals the compiled index by construction (every non-Plaits template).
Shared sources (freq, a velocity param that a kernel also reads, slot/lane constants deduplicated with a kernel mode: constant) are not gate-only and are kept in the elided graph.
A gate whose port-0 subject is itself a source node (such as white-noise) keeps that subject.
A user instrument that appends vactrol-gate keeps its kernel seeds.

Voices that are off, or whose gate lanes are all bypassed, keep the implicit fade and today's lifetime rules. Layer-shaped voices (every gate latched a non-bypassed ping or level) skip ienv and end when every gate reports done.
Cut-group and steal fades still apply to layer-shaped voices.
Gate state resets on in-place rebuild; Template::build stays allocation-free in place; native and wasm32 produce the same ordinals.
mem_total +32, and the budget-minus-one MemExceeded boundaries move with it, in the 14 owned test files. No flexible delay line is clamped at the test budget (24000) or the production budget.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Pre-wiring decay-mod into templates. A user who opts into decay-mod may change that kernel's seed, as documented.
Emulating the upstream trigger delay; any SourcePort fidelity claim or engine coverage change.
Changes to topo_order, assign_mem, the gate memory layout, or the PLV-10/12/20/21 deliverables.
Non-Plaits templates, including the Braids macro-* templates, beyond confirming that their digests are unchanged.
